guideposts.label: Pogacar’s injuries
guideposts.detail: Yesterday, Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) became the first overall leader of La Vuelta to crash out of the race since Igor Anton in 2010. It was Pogacar’s first abandon since Liège-Bastogne-Liège in 2023, and his first ever in a stage race. “Tadej has been diagnosed with a concussion, displaced left clavicle fracture, a stable C7 cervical fracture, and multiple abrasions. Fortunately, no other m

guideposts.label: A very familiar start area
guideposts.detail: Many, many riders are familiar with the area, may it be from the different races held around Valencia and Alicante, or from the training camps teams organise there in the winter season. La Nucia (km 18.1) was home to Spain’s national championships in 2021. Omar Fraile won the men’s elite title ahead of Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH). Mavi Garcia won the women’s title. And Ivan Cobo (Kern Phar

guideposts.label: La Roja
guideposts.detail: Following Pogacar’s crash, Enric Mas (Movistar) leads a Grand Tour for the first time in his career. He is the first Spanish wearer of La Roja since Jesus Herrada wore it for two days in 2018. Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) is second again, a minute behind Mas. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) completes the current podium (+1’11’’) and there are six riders within 2’22’’, with Sepp Kuss (Vis

guideposts.label: Green jersey
guideposts.detail: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) took 20 more points yesterday and now leads the points standings with a tally of 124. He received his 15th green jersey in La Vuelta yesterday, after he claimed 13 in 2024. His teammate Matthew Brennan is second with 67 points. Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) follows with 58 points.

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: Decathlon CMA CGM still lead the team standings with a gap of 12’04’’ on UAE Emirates XRG and 20’35’’ on Visma-Lease a Bike.

guideposts.label: First attacks
guideposts.detail: Nine riders - including Lutsenko, Cort, Johannessen - lead the way after a couple of kilometres. But attacks keep flying and the battle goes on.

guideposts.label: Lutsenko insists
guideposts.detail: The attackers have been reeled in, but Alexey Lutsnko (NSN) attacked again.

guideposts.label: 6 leaders, many counter-attackers
guideposts.detail: Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN), Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility), Alastair Mackellar (EF Education-EasyPost), Fabian Weiss (Tudor) and Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) have opened a gap of 20 seconds at km 9.

guideposts.label: 25 seconds at km 14
guideposts.detail: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) was in pursuit but he's been caught by the bunch.

guideposts.label: Thompson in pursuit
guideposts.detail: Reuben Thompson (Lotto Intermarché) is 25'' behind the six leaders, while the gap to the bunch has increased to 35''.

guideposts.label: 3 chasers, including Cobo
guideposts.detail: As the race passes La Nucia, Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) is chasing with Lennard Kämna (Lidl-Trek) and Reuben Thompson (Lotto Intermarché). Cobo won Spain's U23 national champion title in La Nucia in 2021.

guideposts.label: 25 kilometres of battle
guideposts.detail: Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN), Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility), Alastair Mackellar (EF Education-EasyPost), Fabian Weiss (Tudor) and Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) lead the way. Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma), Lennard Kämna (Lidl-Trek) and Reuben Thompson (Lotto Intermarché) trail by 40''. The gap to the bunch is up to 55''.

guideposts.label: Van Aert accelerates
guideposts.detail: The peloton stretches on the Belgian's wheel. The chasers are caught.

guideposts.label: 5 leaders
guideposts.detail: Fabian Weiss (Tudor) has been distanced by his breakaway companions, who are 5 kilometres from the summit of the first climb.

guideposts.label: Buitrago wants to make the break
guideposts.detail: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) is very active in pursuit of the five leaders.

guideposts.label: Counter-attacks keep flying on the ascent
guideposts.detail: With 3 kilometres remaining on the slopes of Puerto de Tarbena, the gap to the leaders is down to 30 seconds. Carlos Rodriguez (Netcompany Ineos) just accelerated. Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) also sets off.

guideposts.label: Kron leads the way to the first summit
guideposts.detail: The Danish puncheur takes 5 KOM points, ahead of Alessandro Romele (3 pts) and Alexey Lutsenko (1 pt). Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) has accelerated in pursuit.

guideposts.label: Pablo Torres abandons La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: UAE Emirates XRG lose a second rider after Tadej Pogacar's crash yesterday.

guideposts.label: A 4-man chase group 20'' behind the 5 leaders
guideposts.detail: Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma) attacked before the summit and were then joined by Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) and Stefan Küng (Tudor). Movistar drive the bunch on the downhill.

guideposts.label: 41.4 km in the first hour
guideposts.detail: It's been a very intense start with the Puerto de Tarbena and many contenders for the breakaway. And the battle goes on!

guideposts.label: More chasers: Debruyne, Buitrago, Turner...
guideposts.detail: They are still around 20 seconds behind the five leaders after 50 kilometres of battle.

guideposts.label: The second climb of the day
guideposts.detail: The 15 leaders begin the ascent of the Alto del Miserat. Among them, Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) was 2nd behind Brandon McNulty in a stage of the 2024 Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana taht finished on these slopes.

guideposts.label: The situation at the bottom of the second climb
guideposts.detail: Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Pavel Sivakov, Kevin Vermaeke (UAE Emirates XRG), Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike), Embret Svestad-Bardseng (Netcompany Ineos), Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious), Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN Cycling), Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step), Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility), Alastair Mackellar (EF Education-EasyP

guideposts.label: Paret-Peintre: "It's a beautiful stage"
guideposts.detail: Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) has joined the breakaway on roads that inspire him: "It's the stage with the most elevation gain, so we can say it's the queen stage. It's a beautiful stage, it suits me with a long climb at the end, just the way I like it. I like the stage. Of course, [Pogacar's withdrawal] will change the race. Pogacar is the strongest rider in the world, but he also ha

guideposts.label: 18 leaders after 80 km
guideposts.detail: Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step), Marcel Camprubi and Milan Vader (Pinarello-Q36.5) join the front group. Attila Valter (Bahrain Victorious) trails by 40 seconds. Then, Gianni Vermeersch (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Raul Garcia Pierna (Movistar), Pau Marti (NSN), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) and José Manuel Diaz (Burgos Burpellet BH) follow with a gap of 1'05''.

guideposts.label: Valter makes it 19 leaders halfway through the stage
guideposts.detail: Around 45 seconds behind the front group,Gianni Vermeersch (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) has distanced his companions (Garcia Pierna, Marti, Cort, Diaz).

guideposts.label: Vermeersch also joins the front group
guideposts.detail: There are 20 leaders with 89 kilometres to go. The gap to the peloton seems to stabilise at around 5 minutes.

guideposts.label: 24 leaders with 83 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Raul Garcia Pierna (Movistar), Pau Marti (NSN), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), and José Manuel Diaz (Burgos Burpellet BH) are the last entrants, making it a 24-man lead group 4'55'' ahead of the peloton.

guideposts.label: Gall: "It opens a lot of opportunities now"
guideposts.detail: The winner of the queen stage of the Tour de France 2023, Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) is among the riders set to battle at the front today. “I think yesterday, it was… the right word to describe it is a shock", the Austrian climber said at the start. "It felt really unreal to have Tadej [Pogacar] crash out of the race. I wish him all the best for his recovery. That’s cycling also, unfortunately

guideposts.label: Buitrago, a new Colombian with the polka dots?
guideposts.detail: The last Colombian rider to lead the mountains standings of La Vuelta is Nairo Quintana, in 2016. But he was leading the race and thus wearing La Roja, so Spain's Omar Fraile raced with the polka-dot jersey on his behalf. The year before, Colombia's Esteban Chaves led the GC, the points standings and the mountains standings after stage 2. His compatriot Walter Pedraza wore the polka dot jersey the

guideposts.label: Buitrago conquers another summit
guideposts.detail: Results at Puerto de Tudons (cat. 2, km 121.8): 1. Buitrago, 5 pts 2. Calzoni, 3 pts 3. Leemreize, 1 pt

guideposts.label: Langellotti has abandoned
guideposts.detail: The Monaco rider was the hero of the Gran Salida. XDS Astana report he crashed on a downhill.

guideposts.label: More movement in the chase
guideposts.detail: Paret-Peintre and Küng are caught by Vermaerke, Cort and the rest of the chasers. Sivakov accelerates.

guideposts.label: Sivakov joins Camprubi
guideposts.detail: They are 20 seconds behind Romele, who is about to summit.

guideposts.label: Results at the Puerto de Benifallim (cat 2, km 139.9)
guideposts.detail: 1. Romele, 5 pts 2. Sivakov, 3 pts 3. Camprubi, 1 pt

guideposts.label: The 5th summit finish at Alto de Aitana
guideposts.detail: Alto de Aitana is a La Vuelta stage finish for the 5th time, 25 years after the first and 10 years after the last until today. In 2016, it hosted the penultimate finish, on the eve of the Madrid finale. France’s Pierre Latour got the better of Colombia’s Darwin Atapuma at the summit while another Colombian climber, Nairo Quintana, sealed his overall victory against Chris Froome. Riders of La Vuelt

guideposts.label: 3 leaders into the final 40 kilometres
guideposts.detail: Sivakov and Camprubi are with Romele, around 45 seconds ahead of their breakaway rivals. Decathlon CMA CGM have increased the pace in the bunch: 5'40''.

guideposts.label: 16 chasers again
guideposts.detail: Garcia Pierna, Calzoni, Küng, Diaz, Leemreize and Berrade return.

guideposts.label: 30 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Sivakov, Camprubi and Romele still lead the way. +43'' Chase group +5'35'' Peloton

guideposts.label: 2 leaders: Sivakov and Camprubi
guideposts.detail: Romele has been distanced.

guideposts.label: 4 chasers have set off
guideposts.detail: Buitrago, Zana, Lutsenko and Vader have caught up to Romele a minute and a half behind the lead duo.

guideposts.label: 15 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Sivakov and Camprubi still collaborate. +1'05'' Zana, Paret-Peintre, Buitrago, Vader Decathlon CMA CGM have brought the gap to the peloton down to 3'45''.
